_comment: Card CB-Q (docs/SPEC_cb_carry_physical_q.md) leg A — the sat code-bias carry's
process-noise ladder.  ONE KNOB differs across the five arms:
filter.process_noise.sat_code_bias_q.  Everything else is inherited from
the Jul-28 armed set), cut to 600 s = 20 epochs.
PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTIONS (the point of the leg is to be wrong in public):
P1  ctl vs hw: max |delta code_bias| over every emitted B record <= 1 mm.
q*dt is 3e-9 vs 1.2e-6 m^2 against a MEASURED typical cb fold variance of
2.2e-4 m^2, so both are inert and 'set q to hardware physics' is a no-op.
P2  the first rung whose max |delta| exceeds 1 cm lies between 1e-6 and 7.3e-6.
P3  the cb variance factor (constraint-aware global sigma0, run-end) changes by
LESS THAN 2x even at 1e-4 — because the row's redundancy r = 1 - w*v is
0.0186, i.e. R ~ 53*P, so inflating P cannot move (R+sigma_t^2)/(P+R).
If P3 fails, the inertness arithmetic in the SPEC is wrong.
FRESH lineage; own paths; run alone (scripts/q3_ladder_run.ps1 serializes).
rung 2 — just below the derived fold-variance knee.
